dataset_metadata.title: Mississippi Commercial Truck Digital Evidence Guide
dataset_metadata.methodology: Attorney-edited data dictionary derived from current official federal regulations and public manufacturer or vendor documentation. Product capabilities are paraphrased and linked; no proprietary manual, client file, discovery production, or commercial database text is reproduced.
important_limitations: A listed capability does not prove that the capability was installed, enabled, subscribed to, functioning, recorded, retained, or retrievable in a particular vehicle or event.
Vehicle, hardware, firmware, account settings, connectivity, power, retention settings, and custodian practices can change available data.

Federal regulatory retention periods are minimum recordkeeping rules for defined records, not guaranteed lifespans for every electronic artifact and not safe waiting periods for litigation preservation.
This dataset contains no real case, client, claimant, opposing party, settlement, medical, police-report, or discovery data.
dataset_metadata.disclaimer: General educational information only; not legal advice or an expert evidence opinion. Verify current law, product documentation, vehicle configuration, and case-specific facts.

records.name: Electronic logging device records and records of duty status
custodian_examples: ELD service provider, depending on contract and system architecture
possible_data_categories: location information required by the ELD specification
edits, annotations, certifications, malfunctions, and diagnostic events

federal_minimum_retention.period: not less than 6 months from the motor carrier's receipt

preservation_questions: Which ELD make, model, registration, account, and driver profile applied?
Were unassigned-driving, edits, annotations, diagnostics, and original export files preserved?
Which supporting documents can be matched to the driver's record of duty status?
records.availability_note: The precise fields and export format depend on the applicable ELD specification, device, account, and record. Confirm the current eCFR text and the registered device documentation.

records.name: ELD backup records
possible_data_categories: backup copy of driver ELD records on a device separate from the original storage
preservation_questions: Where was the separate backup maintained?
Does the preserved export include metadata, edits, annotations, and diagnostic events?
records.availability_note: The rule addresses backup and security of ELD records; it does not describe every vendor's separate operational, portal, video, or telematics retention setting.

records.name: Detroit Assurance with Active Brake Assist 5
related_platforms_to_investigate: fleet safety reports and event notifications
preservation_questions: What exact Detroit Assurance generation, features, hardware, calibration, and software were present?
Was Detroit Connect enabled and, if so, which events or reports were transmitted?
Were diagnostic downloads, warning/intervention records, fault codes, calibration, repair, and configuration records preserved?
records.availability_note: The official product pages describe safety features and connected-safety reporting. They do not establish that any specific collision generated a stored, downloadable event or that every listed field exists. Obtain vehicle- and account-specific documentation.

records.name: Bendix Wingman Fusion
records.system_class: integrated advanced driver-assistance and collision-mitigation system
publicly_described_inputs_or_features: overspeed alerts or intervention on configured systems
related_platforms_to_investigate: fleet safety-event reports and triggered video when configured
preservation_questions: Which Wingman Fusion generation and OEM-specific feature set was installed?
Was SafetyDirect or another camera/event platform connected and subscribed?
Were radar/camera/brake faults, calibrations, interventions, triggered clips, and fleet alerts preserved?
records.availability_note: Bendix states that truck manufacturers may implement different feature sets. Public descriptions do not prove that a specific event or clip was stored or retrievable.

records.name: Geotab GO9
publicly_described_data_or_features: collision data buffer described in the GO9 support document
records.public_memory_description: Geotab's GO9 support document describes up to 80,000 offline logs, a buffer of more than 100 minutes of second-by-second collision data, and immediate transmission of the last 72 records (1.2 minutes) for accelerometer-triggered collision-level events.
preservation_questions: What GO device model, serial number, harness, firmware, plan, and vehicle assignment applied?
What raw logs, collision reconstruction data, exceptions, trips, GPS, accelerometer, engine, and audit records exist?
Was the device powered, connected, calibrated, moved, replaced, or removed around the event?
records.availability_note: The support document describes device capabilities, not proof that a specific account retained or transmitted each field. Vehicle compatibility, triggers, coverage, power, configuration, and account retention affect availability.

records.name: Samsara Vehicle Gateway
publicly_described_data_or_features: real-time and historical tracking of sensor data
ELD, trip, route, and vehicle integrations depending on configuration and license
preservation_questions: Which Vehicle Gateway model, serial number, cable, license, driver/vehicle assignment, and settings applied?
Which trips, GPS points, harsh events, diagnostics, HOS, dispatch, messages, camera clips, and audit logs exist in the account?
Was the vehicle deleted, deactivated, transferred, unplugged, in low-power mode, or outside coverage?
records.availability_note: Samsara documentation distinguishes deactivation, transfer, and deletion and describes configuration-dependent functionality. A device or account may not capture or retain every proposed field. Preserve the account and identify the exact model/settings promptly.

records.name: Fleet dispatch, safety, and driver communications
custodian_examples: fleet-management, messaging, email, telephone, or collaboration service provider
possible_data_categories: delay, fatigue, maintenance, or safety reports
message delivery/read status and audit metadata where available
preservation_questions: Which channels, accounts, devices, groups, and custodians communicated with the driver?
Were messages exportable with timestamps, participants, edits, attachments, delivery/read state, and time zone?
What warning sources did leadership monitor, and how were warnings escalated to dispatchers and drivers?
records.availability_note: No single federal retention period covers every communication system or business record. Retention can vary by platform, contract, account setting, carrier policy, custodian action, and litigation hold.

records.name: Commercial-vehicle and third-party video ecosystem
possible_data_categories: vehicle, warehouse, loading-dock, roadway, and nearby surveillance video
preservation_questions: Which cameras recorded continuously, on a trigger, locally, or in the cloud?
What pre-event and post-event windows, audio, overlays, sensor metadata, and original file hashes exist?
Were clips viewed, tagged, downloaded, shared, edited, deleted, or subject to a retention policy?
records.availability_note: Video retention is highly system- and custodian-specific. A clipped or transcoded copy may omit surrounding footage or metadata. Seek native exports and document chain of custody.
